author: rdc-rfc1-author-a (Claude Haiku 5.5)
rationale: core_rst_n = por_n & wdt_rst_n clears q_a in clk_a, but wdt_rst_n is a clk_b flop, so the clk_a reset releases on clk_b edges with no clk_a synchroniser while q_a may capture beat.

author_reading.rationale: clk_b's wdt_rst_n is combined with por_n and drives the asynchronous clear of clk_a flops, so the clk_a reset releases on clk_b edges with no synchroniser in clk_a.

labels.rationale: core_rst_n = por_n & wdt_rst_n is a reset for clk_a logic, but wdt_rst_n is a single clk_b flop (D=1) with no clk_a synchroniser. Its release is unsynchronised to clk_a, so q_a can be released unsafely. Clocks are declared asynchronous.
With POR inactive, a clk_b flip-flop directly releases core_rst_n. The clocks are asynchronous, so the release can violate recovery or removal of q_a.
labels.suspected_flaw: The clk_b beat register also has direct POR release and an unrelated asynchronous data capture.

settlement.rationale: Both readers are right on verdict, class and the clk_b-generated reset. RDC-007 is the rule that targets a reset generated in another clock domain. RDC-009 (A) targets glitchy gating rather than this release, RDC-003 (B) defers register-generated resets from another domain to RDC-007, and RDC-002 is an incidental inventory warning. Sites follow A; q_a (B) is the victim, not the defect.
